newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Buyers of Venezuela's CVG to assume debt service.
newsitem.headline: Buyers of Venezuela's CVG to assume debt service.

text.p: The buyers in Venezuela's $3 billion privatizations of aluminum and steel units of (Parastatal Corporacion Venezolana de Guayana or CVG slated for later this year will assume responsibility for servicing those companies' large debts, a government minister said.

"The aluminum sector's total debts are around $1.2 billion, and iron company Sidor's debt is around $650 million," Venezuelan Investment Fund (FIV) president Alberto Poletto, with portfolio for privatization, told Reuters in an exclusive interview.

"The buyers will take on those debts, but they won't have to pay them off as a condition of the sale," he said. "That would have deterred a number of investors. The investor will assume the costs of servicing those debts."
Of the aluminum sector's debts, half are with the government and half with commercial banks. Sidor's debt is solely with the Venezuelan government.
How to best treat the debts has been a sticking point in the run-up to the companies' expected sale, but Poletto said the latest mechanism had recently been approved by the Executive.
CVG is the holding company for steel producer Sidor, as well as for four aluminum companies -- smelters Venalum and Alcasa, bauxite producer Bauxilum and carbon anode producer Carbonorca.
Thirteen companies have qualified to bid for the four aluminum companies in CVG, including Aluminum Co of America, Gencor Ltd, Alumax Inc, Reynolds Metals Co, Norsk Hydro A/S and RTZ Corp Plc.

Eleven companies have also qualified for Sidor's sale, inlcuding Mexcio's Hylsamex SA, Imexsa, and Ahmsa; Brazil's Usiminas and Companhia Siderugica Nacional ; Japan's Kobe Steel ; Argentina's Rand Siderar SAIC ; and Venezuela's Sivensa.
